voyage.name: Jet d'Eau
voyage.hours: daily 10:00-23:00 (shut off in November for maintenance and during strong winds.)
voyage.content: One of the crowning symbols of Geneva is the monumental Jet d'Eau, a fountain of water pumped 140m into the air. The spectacular plume was once an occasional pressure release for hydro-power generation on the Rhône River, but people liked it so much that in 1891 the city created a permanent pumped fountain. It's beautifully lit at night. Best viewed from a distance — the surrounding half kilometer is soaked with wate

voyage.name: Cathédrale St-Pierre and Calvin's auditorium
voyage.price: Adults Fr. 16 (Seniors, Disabled, Students aged 16-25, and groups of more than 15 qualify for a Fr. 10 pass, children aged 7-16 qualify for an Fr. 8 pass. Entry to the church itself is free, of course, but donations are welcome.)
voyage.content: The new Espace Saint Pierre pass includes entrance to all three sites of Cour Saint-Pierre, a worthy space of unique spiritual and cultural importance. The Cathedral and its towers, originally Catholic, both embody the high point of the Reformed tradition and explore the origins of Christianity with an extensive archaeological site and they are now complemented by the International Museum of the Reformation on the gr

voyage.name: Old Town
voyage.content: Aside of the cathedral the Old town in general is worth walking around in for an hour or two. Among the highlights are the city hall with the cannons in the little square opposite to it, Rousseau's birth house and various antique shops with all sorts of interesting stuff in the windows. A word of warning to people with physical disabilities: the Old Town, is situated on a hill with quite steep streets leading up to i

voyage.name: Palais des Nations
voyage.price: Fr. 12 each for adults (groups of 20 adults or more qualify for a 20% discount; private tour of 1-14 adults Fr. 127.50; Fr. 10 each for students, senior citizens, and disabled persons; Fr. 4 for schoolchildren; free for children under six years old)
voyage.hours: Open daily Apr-Oct: 10:00-12:00 and 14:00-16:00; Jul-Aug 10:00-17:00; the rest of the year Mon-Fri 10:00-12:00 and 14:00-16:00 (except over the Christmas period)
voyage.content: Built to house the League of Nations, the Palais is worth visiting just to take in the magnificent Assembly Hall, in addition to the large collection of public art, the library, and the landscaped grounds. Visits are by guided tours only. For most of the year there are two or four of them per day, in the summer months they are arranged depending on the number of visitors. Enter the complex at the Appia gate, and go t

voyage.name: Quartier des Grottes
voyage.content: An area with interesting shops and most importantly, a series of residential buildings called "les Schtroumpfs" (1982-1984), where the architects tried to avoid all straight lines, leading to an unconventional Gaudi-like appearance.

voyage.name: Monument Brunswick
voyage.content: An impressive monument, constructed in 1873 as a Mausoleum for the Duke of Brunswick, as a replica of the tomb of the Scaligeri family in Verona (14th century). Also worth visiting for the 5-star hotels and the cars in front of them.

voyage.name: Île Rousseau
voyage.content: Small island where the lake ends and river Rhône begins named after the famous philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau - of course there's a statue of him there too.

voyage.name: L'Ile
voyage.content: Worth visiting for the old Tour de L'Ile, the remains of a fortified castle erected in the 13th century.

voyage.name: Place Neuve
voyage.content: See the impressive Grand Theatre (1879, renovated after a fire in 1951), the Conservatoire de musique, and the Musée Rath. Also visit the Parc des Bastions, which includes a large wall ("Mur des Réformateurs") showing some of the famous people of the Reformation movement.

voyage.name: Eaux-Vives
voyage.content: While many of Geneva's buildings are similar in style to what you would find in French cities, the Mairie of Eaux-Vives is a great example of the typical Swiss architecture you would find in cities like Zürich. If you're interested in modern architecture, also visit Rue Saint-Laurent for "La Clarté", an avant-garde building designed by Le Corbusier in 1931/32 — one of 17 Le Corbusier buildings to be listed on the UNE

voyage.name: Carouge
voyage.content: A district of Geneva that once belonged to the Kingdom of Sardinia and hence retains a distinct Italian flavour.

voyage.name: Jardin botanique
voyage.content: At the botanical garden you can see flowers, plants and trees both from the Alps and from other parts of the world. The palm house also hosts tropical vegetation. In the northern part of the park there is a zoo spread over a quite large area with birds and some Alpine mammals such as goats and deer.

voyage.name: International Museum of the Reformation
voyage.price: Fr. 10 for Adults; Seniors, Disabled, Students from 16-25 years old qualify for a Fr. 7 admission fee; Children age 7-16 years old and groups of 15 or more qualify for a Fr. 5 admission fee; Children under 7 are free. For another Fr. 3, you can explore the archaeological site beneath the cathedral and climb the tower inside the cathedral, which has some amazing views of the city
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00. Closed on 24, 25 and 31 December and on 1 January. Open Easter, Pentecost, and Jeune Federal Mondays. Access for disabled visitors.
voyage.content: Installed on the ground floor of the magnificent Maison Mallet (next to Saint-Pierre Cathedral), this new Museum presents the main spiritual and cultural elements of the Reformation. Unique objects, manuscripts, rare books, engravings, and paintings illustrate the close ties between Geneva and the Reformation. State-of-the-art technology welcomes a modern audience: films, a music room, and demonstrations, including m

voyage.name: Museum of the International Committee of the Red Cross
voyage.price: Adult Fr. 15; child, ICRC members, the elderly, and others Fr. 7
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00. Closed on 24, 25 and 31 December and on 1 January. Access for disabled visitors.
voyage.content: The Museum of the ICRC is in the basement of the headquarters and shows photos and objects related to the organisation's service to humanity during countless wars and natural disasters, and presents stories of victims. However much of the permanent exhibition is not an ordinary museum, but probably supposed to be more of an "experience", one might even call it a theme park — not really appropriate for such a serious

voyage.name: Musée Ariana
voyage.content: Occupying a big chunk of what would otherwise be the UN campus, the Ariana Museum offers a huge collection (16,000 pieces) of ceramics from around Europe and the Far East.

voyage.name: Musée d'Art Moderne et Contemporain
voyage.content: Late modern, post-modern, and contemporary works by internationally known artists, as well as a special collection of Swiss conceptual work.

voyage.name: Musée d'Histoire Naturelle
voyage.content: Geneva has a nice museum which is worth a visit, especially if you have youth and children.

voyage.name: Musée d'Art et d'Histoire
voyage.content: Extensive art and archaeological-historical collections. Painting gallery extends back to the early Renaissance, but is most extensive in Swiss-French and Impressionist works.

voyage.name: Fondation Baur, Musée des Arts d’Extrême-Orient
voyage.content: The largest collections of Far Eastern art open to the public in Switzerland. Temporary exhibitions are regularly organized several times a year.

voyage.name: Patek Philippe Museum
voyage.price: Adults Fr. 10, Seniors/people with disabilities/unemployed/students Fr. 7, under 18 years old free
voyage.content: Four floors of stunningly beautiful watches and clocks from the last centuries, both Patek Philippe and other brands. There is also a section presenting watchmaking in practice. Bags (even shopping bags) must be kept in free lockers so don't arrive with suitcases!

voyage.name: CERN Science Gateway
voyage.content: The CERN particle physics research centre has a purpose built museum presenting the history of CERN, our universe and quantum science at a level accessible to all. Almost all exhibits are interactive and are presented in five languages (French, English, German, Italian and Spanish). There are also workshops for children (free, 45 mins) and guided tours (90 mins) of the premises which can only be booked on site. The r

voyage.name: Musée d'histoire des sciences
voyage.content: Museum dedicated to scientists who've lived and worked in Geneva. You can see old equipment from telescopes to galvanometers and glass eyes.

voyage.name: Maison Tavel
voyage.content: Three floors presenting the history of Geneva from the Middle Ages until the 19th century. There's an entrance fee to the temporary exhibitions in the basement.

voyage.name: Salève cable car
voyage.content: Just over the French border, this high alpine ridge has a stunning view of Mt. Blanc and the Lake Geneva area and miles of walking trails. A cute little corner shop in Pas de l'Échelle Village (France) sells about 100 varieties of French cheeses and is open on Sundays. Don't forget your passport.

voyage.name: Association Genevoise des Amis du Salève
voyage.content: Organizes free hikes around Geneva every Sunday. Start at 10:00 (sharp) at terminus (End station) of bus number 8 at Veyrier-Douane.

voyage.name: Genève Plage
voyage.content: There are many smaller places where to swim in either the rivers or the lake, but the largest one is Genève Plage (literally "Geneva Beach") at the eastern bank of the lake. It's a nice place to swim, enjoy the sun, play, barbecue, or just hang out.

voyage.name: International Geneva Motor Show
voyage.address: in the Palexpo centre next to the airport

voyage.name: Caves Ouvertes
voyage.content: Free annual event. Sample wine at Geneva's wineries while exploring the canton's rural side.

voyage.name: Bol d'Or
voyage.content: Yacht Race (biggest in Europe).

voyage.name: Fête de la Musique
voyage.content: For three days in June, the whole City of Geneva is a stage. Actually, there are on the order of 40 of them. The musical offerings include children's choirs, punk rock, chamber orchestras, jam bands, avant-guard jazz, klezmer, and drum and bass DJs. The venues are as diverse as the music, with stages inside and out of l'Usine, Parc des Bastions, and even Cathédral St. Pierre. There is also a wide assortment of intern

voyage.name: Fêtes de la Batie
voyage.content: A 16-day arts festival (usually starts the last weekend of July and through most of August) with installations and live shows in over 20 venues across the city. Very similar in feel to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival. 2025 is operating from 28 Aug to 14 Sep.

voyage.name: L'Escalade
voyage.content: Running and walking competitions open to everybody.

voyage.name: Parc des Bastions
voyage.address: entrance at Place Neuve or just down rue St. Léger from Place Bourg de Four.
voyage.content: This lovely tree lined park, which is home to the liberal arts campus of the University of Geneva features giant chessboards and even larger statues of Geneva's Calvinist founding fathers, and it's directly between the old town and Plain de Plainpalais, so it makes a good transitional area for exploring.

voyage.name: Parc des Eaux Vives
voyage.address: entrance at the far end of Rue des Eaux Vives and the number 2 bus line. There's also a boat dock, with service from the Pâquis
voyage.content: This park offers promenades and views over the lake of the UN campus and the Palais des Nations. Geneva beach is at the end furthest from the city, on the lakefront.

voyage.name: Parc de la Grange
voyage.content: Just along the south side of the Lake Geneva promenade, Parc de la Grange is a large park which contains a rose garden, a historic mansion and a tree-lined path leading to the nearby Parc des Eaux Vives.

voyage.name: Bois de la Bâtie
voyage.content: Just over the river Arve from Jonction. Most of this woodsy bluff has been left in a more-or-less natural state, though there are walking trails around the edges. The trails connect eventually with a sidewalk which crosses a railroad bridge to the St. Jean neighborhood. There is also a small (free) zoo at the western edge of the woods. If you don't like to walk up the trail from the river you can take the bus up to C

voyage.name: Jardin Anglais
voyage.content: A small park where people like to spend their lunch break. Located at the bank of Lake Geneva, just as you've crossed over the Mont Blanc bridge to the southern half of the city. In the summer there are many small concerts and funfairs held in the park, especially around at the time of the "city party" Fête de Gèneve. Don't miss the flower decorated clock at the southwestern edge of the park.

voyage.name: La Perle du Lac
voyage.content: Translates to the "Pearl of the Lake" and is the largest park on the western bank of Lake Geneva. It hosts the splendid eponymous restaurant and a free science museum, but it also a great place for a picnic.

voyage.name: Manor
voyage.content: A department store in the city centre where you can buy clothes, food, electronics etc. There is a self service restaurant on the top floor.

voyage.name: Centre Commercial Cygnes
voyage.content: A variety of smaller shops and eateries under one roof a short walk along Rue de Lausanne from the railway station.

voyage.name: Flea market at Plainpalais
voyage.content: If you like flea markets and shuffling through old stuff like vinyl records, books, chinaware etc., especially stuff with a Swiss and French background and happen to be in Geneva on a Saturday (or some Wednesdays), Plainpalais square is definitely where you should head.

voyage.name: Buvette des Bains (Bains des Paquis)
voyage.content: Wonderful place in the middle of the lake. Beach in Summer, fondue restaurant in Winter. Good "plat du jour" all day for Fr. 12

voyage.name: Espresso Club
voyage.content: A tiny bar and three tables means this little local spot is usually packed with a very international crowd of people who know where to get the best pizza, salads, and pasta dishes in town, with many vegetarian selections. Espresso club keeps the ovens going late for late working customers and it's a nice spot for a café and newspaper afternoon as well. Unfortunately the quality of its customer service does not mirror

voyage.name: Café Art's
voyage.content: Café Art's (sic) has a limited menu of salads and pasta dishes, but all around or under Fr. 15 and service is non-stop all day.

voyage.name: Sing Fa la maison du Ravioli (Sing Fa dumpling house)
voyage.hours: morning-midnight (closed on Mon lunch), opened 7 days a week
voyage.content: Serves fairly authentic Chinese dumplings and noodles.

voyage.name: Asia Garden
voyage.content: Large selection of Chinese and Japanese dishes. Quality Chinese food (it's always full of Chinese customers) but no fancy atmosphere.

voyage.name: Piment Vert
voyage.content: Indian and Sri Lankan fast food in a charmingly appointed space. There's also a terrace during warm weather.

voyage.name: Chez Ma Cousine
voyage.content: A chain with a simple menu: chicken, chicken, or chicken. The roasted chicken is what they're famous for, and two chicken salads make the rest of the regular menu, each under Fr. 14.90.

voyage.name: Ali Haydar
voyage.content: Serves kebabs of lamb, chicken, or both, dolma. Baklava too.

voyage.name: Cafe Istanbul
voyage.content: Turkish kebab house.

voyage.name: Manora
voyage.content: Cafeteria like serving area with everything and anything including (but not inclusive): chicken, pasta, pizza, desserts, entree of the day, salads, and coffee. Great view of the Geneva skyline from the balcony eating area.

voyage.name: Wasabi Sushi
voyage.address: 21 rue du Mont Blanc, 32 Boulevard Helvetique
voyage.content: As the name suggests, Japanese food to eat in the restaurant or to take away.

voyage.name: Boulangerie Tea-Room Deux-Ponts
voyage.content: Portuguese "tea room" serving sandwiches, bifanas (hot sandwiches) and pastries that are fresh, delicious, large and don't cost very much. The catch: they don't have very much on display so you can't just point at stuff but need to explain what you would like to order and how you'd like it - in French or Portuguese!

voyage.name: La feuille de banane
voyage.content: One of the best ratios of food quality to price in Geneva for Asiatic food. For around Fr. 10, you can have a tasty meal with chicken, beef or fish, and various choices of sauces. The service is ultra fast since everything is already cooked, but yet fresh and tasty.

voyage.name: Restaurant La Romana
voyage.content: Restaurant, pizzeria, bar, karaoké, cocktail and private party.

voyage.name: Gives a Fork
voyage.content: Vegetarian and vegan Asian food with a tasting menu and interesting cocktails

voyage.name: Café de Paris
voyage.price: You can buy the butter in 250 g (0.5 lb) for Fr. 18. The menu costs Fr. 42 per person.
voyage.content: Vegetarians beware, this Genevois favourite serves one dish only: steak with the butter sauce that bears the name of the restaurant, French fries, and salad. But apparently they do it very well.

voyage.name: Café du Soleil
voyage.content: This ancient Petit Saconnex roadhouse claims to be possibly the oldest restaurant in Geneva and to have probably the best fondue in Switzerland. They have a nice large patio in front that is overlooked by a 2nd floor balcony with a few small tables and also inside seating. Surprisingly popular even if it's in a mostly residential part of Geneva, even among international guests.

voyage.name: Café Gourmand
voyage.content: Great friendly atmosphere specializing in East-West fusion dishes. Open weekdays.

voyage.name: Le Comptoir
voyage.content: Easy-Listener-chic Asian/fusion restaurant and bar sporting white leather sofas and the occasional local DJ. Not a cheap choice, but the food is unusually interesting and the crowd friendly.

voyage.name: L'Europa
voyage.content: A little hard to find, but worth it for the fresh, hand made pasta dishes and generous portions. A favourite for lunch among the UN crowd.

voyage.name: Hashimoto
voyage.content: Hashimoto Sushi is a favourite spot for Japanese diplomats and international civil servants in Geneva, which should tell you enough.

voyage.name: L'Adresse
voyage.content: Self-consciously hip but decent food. Occasionally snooty service.

voyage.name: L'Entrecôte Couronnée
voyage.content: Excellent steak restaurant with fast and efficient staff. The wine card is limited but has good Swiss wines. Just 40 seats so better reserve a table

voyage.name: La Table du 9
voyage.hours: 12:00-14:00 & 19:00-22:00, closed on Saturdays and Sundays, and for dinner on Mon and Tue
voyage.content: Relaxed, modern and justifiably busy.

voyage.name: Edward's The fine art of sandwiches
voyage.content: Packed with locals at lunchtime and for a reason - delicious warm sandwiches and cakes. On the downside it is a bit hectic and it might be difficult to find a seat.

voyage.name: Brasserie Bagatelle
voyage.price: main course and glass of wine Fr. 30
voyage.content: A centrally located restaurant with a varied menu and moderate prices for being in the middle of Geneva. Really good tartar with French fries.

voyage.name: Le Montparnasse
voyage.price: mains Fr. 20-40, but has lunch specials and the three-course "Menu of the day" for Fr. 30
voyage.content: French and Swiss cuisine and a healthy "antidote" to the extremely touristy restaurants serving Swiss food. Most of the visitors are older locals who drop in for a few glasses of wine and a chat with the owner. Try the menu of the day and a good local wine!

voyage.name: La Cuccagna
voyage.content: Cosy Italian restaurant in Carouge with a wide variety of well known and lesser known Italian dishes and even occasionally live music. The service is a bit slow but the ambience so you won't probably mind sitting there for a little bit longer.

voyage.name: Brasserie Lipp
voyage.content: Good brasserie, lots of seafood.

voyage.name: Café des Négociants
voyage.content: Wonderful hip restaurant with wonderful hip food and a wonderful hip wine cellar where you can wander around and choose from all the wonderful hip wine on the racks. You can guess what the desserts are like. Everyone wants a piece of this place, so plan to reserve up to a week or so in advance.

voyage.name: Da Renato
voyage.content: Italian-style restaurant.

voyage.name: Edelweiss Manotel
voyage.content: This is a must if you want to taste the Swiss culture. You will get the cheese fondue, of course, but also some other local delicacies. But you get there for the show: you can hear and see folklore music and yodelling singers, as well as many other instruments. It is however a very touristic restaurant and you are not likely to see many Swiss people eating there.

voyage.name: Perle du Lac
voyage.price: Fr. 65 (lunch), from Fr. 88 for set menu
voyage.content: The only restaurant located adjacent to the Lake Geneva footpath. Food and service are excellent. The view of the Lake is excellent and the ambiance is outstanding.

voyage.name: Le Triporteur
voyage.content: This little place fills a nice niche at the low end of the high end, where it is likely to impress the heck out of a date without overly denting the bank account. The room is cosy and romantic. The service is attentive, but not at all pushy or snobbish. The Triporteur has the feel of a lot of the better restaurants in say, San Francisco. Expect to spend around Fr. 50 per person if you're drinking the house wine.

voyage.name: La Veranda
voyage.content: A pleasant restaurant with Italian flair in the Hotel International-Terminus.

voyage.name: Les Brasseurs
voyage.hours: Tue to Sat until 02:00, Sun and Mon until 00:00
voyage.content: One of the few brew pubs in Geneva, Les Brass serves three flavours of home brew in the usual half pints, pints, and litre glasses or you can go for one of the giant plastic tubes filled with three to five litres. A small menu of pub food and a full restaurant in the back makes it a good spot to waste an evening.

voyage.name: Café de la Gare
voyage.content: Of the two restaurants attached to the Hotel Montbrillant this is the pick. The beautifully decorated but unpretentious Café de la Gare captures the laid-back feel of some of the best sidewalk cafés in Paris. It's a great place for dinner as well, with excellent Swiss, French, and Italian offerings.

voyage.name: Pickwicks
voyage.content: One of the half-dozen or so British pubs, Pickwicks claims to be the largest pub in Switzerland. Usually full of football watching expats eating fish and chips while sipping Guinness. Friday and Saturday night usually features live music. A laid-back, friendly spot. One of the best in Geneva for burgers and a dozen draft beers!

voyage.name: Alhambar
voyage.content: A swanky cocktail bar above the Alhambra Theater. Pretty people in a pretty room, usually with a DJ. A small tapas menu early in the evening and a nice brunch on weekends until 14:00.

voyage.name: La Clémence
voyage.content: This cozy little bar on the central square of Geneva's old town more than quintuples in size from April until October when it is able to use a huge swath of the place as its terrace. During warm weather it's packed, but is such a lovely and central stopping point that it's worth the wait for a table - check out the gallery on their website. In the winter they have the best vin chaud in town.

voyage.name: Café Demi-Lune
voyage.content: Located in a small street connecting to Place du Bourg-de-Four (Old town), this little café has a very charming attitude and atmosphere. A good place for after dinner drinks with good friends.

voyage.name: Saveurs & Couleurs Café
voyage.content: The Grottes neighbourhood of Geneva has long been a centre for creative types, many of whom can be found of an evening enjoying a glass of wine at this comfy little bistro.

voyage.name: Boréal Coffee Shop
voyage.content: This cozy coffee shop is in the bank district. Espressos, Cappuccinos, Lattes, Renversés, Macchiatos, Mochacinos, ice coffees and teas can be consumed there or take-away. The coffee is great, there is a free WIFI connection. This is the kind of places where you feel like staying hours, lovely!

voyage.name: Les Enfants Terribles
voyage.content: A café bar bicycle-workshop hair salon and wine shop, with a nice lunch tapas buffet and Thursday night jazz in a beautiful post-industrial space with atrium roofs and an olive tree. What is there not to like?

voyage.name: Grand Duke Pub
voyage.content: One of the oldest English pubs in Geneva. Live sports, wide selection of draught and bottled beers, ciders. More than 5 big television screens are there to watch different sports as well as a good area to play darts. You can enjoy watching sports such as NFL, NBA, Masters Tennis, Football League, Boxing, MLB, NHL, Premier League, and International Rugby union. Also serves lunch specials, burgers, steaks, salads and c

voyage.name: Mulligans Irish Pub
voyage.content: You will be guaranteed a great time at this centrally located pub. Good music most nights. Bands often play on Thursday and Friday evenings. A good lively crowd who know how to party. Guinness, Bulmers, Staropramen, Boddingtons, spirits, shots.

voyage.name: Remor
voyage.content: Really the best Parisien-style grande café in Geneva. Artwork by University Students and sometimes the Proprietor hang on the wall. They also offer two salads of the day, and a range of ice-cream treats. They screen the best of Swiss film, for free. Fr. 3.50/5.00 draft/bottle beers. Free Wi-fi available.

voyage.name: Le Ferblanterie
voyage.price: Fr. 3/6 draft/bottle beers. A glass of wine is about the same
voyage.content: The Ferblanterie, or Tinsmith would be one of the coolest bars in just about any town, and it happens to be on a street loaded with cool bars. This is very much a student haunt, and a grungy one in all the right ways. Some of the CDs in the rack above the CD player are by Paulo Conté, Tom Waits, Fugazi, the Art Ensemble of Chicago, and Charles Mingus, if that tells you anything.

voyage.name: L'Etabli
voyage.price: Fr. 3/6 draft/bottle beers. A glass of wine is about the same.
voyage.content: L'Etabli is a great place to go when the Ferblanterie is packed, or perhaps it's the other way around. This super-friendly little café/bar/wine bar is a great place to meet grad students to help with your French, or to help with their English, or just to argue politics or whatever.

voyage.name: Bypass
voyage.content: One of the most modern clubs in Geneva, the Bypass is, for lack of a better word, bling-bling. The dance floor swarms with young professionals and, on occasion, corporate parties and the rooms pound with clean house music, hip-hop and R'n'B. This club is not near the city centre, but still just a short taxi ride from it.

voyage.name: Java Club
voyage.content: Inside the Grand Hotel Kempinski

voyage.name: Shakers
voyage.content: This club is known for the wild nights within, thanks to its very strong cocktails served in shaker glasses. The dance floor is imposing, but once on it, well known for romantic encounters. Very popular with English speakers.

voyage.name: Weetamix
voyage.content: Although it's not the easiest place to get to, Weetamix is able to attract good, mostly local crowds by consistently booking some of the best cutting-edge talent in electronic music from France, Britain, and the U.S..

voyage.name: The Zoo at l'Usine
voyage.content: See Moloko Bar under Drink or their homepage.

voyage.name: Youth Hostel Geneva
voyage.content: A clean well maintained place. Well placed for access to the bars and restaurants of the Paquis, and only a 15-minute walk from the central station. Floors, lockers, and doors, unfortunately, are all fairly loud, and if staying in a shared room, you must bring ear plugs.

voyage.name: City Hostel Geneva
voyage.price: Laundry, internet, lockers and communal kitchens are available for two to four person dormitories (Fr. 28 and up) as well as single (Fr. 63 and up) and double rooms (Fr. 70 and up)
voyage.content: A clean and hassle-free, if somewhat soul-less, hostel located near the budget food haven of Paquis and the central train station.

voyage.name: Cité Universitaire
voyage.content: A huge dorm space with 500 beds, which means that if all else fails you can probably sleep here and it's cheap. It is a bit far out of the old town though, about 2 km south on the bluff of Champel, which overlooks the Arve river across from Carouge. However, is right next to the crets de Champel line 3 stop. Because it is not a hotel, the reception closes at 21:00. Call first to make sure that there is availability.

voyage.name: Hotel Formule 1
voyage.address: Route de Meyrin, 01210 Ferney Voltaire, France
voyage.content: Right behind the airport on the French side. Inexpensive but still a good standard since it belongs to the Accor hotel chain. Walls are thin. Decorations are cute. Breakfast is available for an additional Fr. 4. It can be difficult to get to by public transit (bus to the roundabout next to the shopping centre from Meyrin-Graviere stop, line 14) and it's a Fr. 40 taxi trip from the airport, so it's probably best for g

voyage.name: Hotel de Geneve
voyage.content: 5-minute walk from Cornavin Station, 4 bus stops away from St. Pierre Cathedral.

voyage.name: Hotel Residence St.James
voyage.content: The St-James Residence is in an elegant district in the centre of town on a street parallel with the River Rhone.

voyage.name: Eastwest
voyage.content: Modern 4-star for business travellers and tourists. Good central location, nice neighbourhood for a late drink. 41 rooms & suites.

voyage.name: Hotel Lido
voyage.content: Simple 2-star close to the train station and outside the red-light district.

voyage.name: Le Montbrillant
voyage.content: This lovely hotel is in an excellent location. Try to get a room on the top floor under the sloping roof. With two good restaurants: Café de la Gare and a pizzeria.

voyage.name: Hôtel Bel'Espérance
voyage.content: 3-star run by the Salvation Army, the Bel'Espérance is less hotel like than many hotels; they have a little kitchen with small individual refrigerators if you want to cook, and considering how close the hotel is to the Wednesday morning farmer's market on blvd Helvetique there's a pretty good chance you will want to. You can take your meals on the rooftop terrace or in the big, comfy lounge area.

voyage.name: Hotel Strasbourg
voyage.content: Very central 3-star hotel. The desk staff are very knowledgeable and helpful.

voyage.name: Hôtel-Résidence du Grand-Saconnex
voyage.content: Cheapest available in Geneva near airport. Studio or standard rooms. Restaurant serves Swiss and Serbian food.

voyage.name: Bernina
voyage.content: Three-star hotel, very central.

voyage.name: Hotel Drake Longchamp
voyage.content: 3-star hotel, member of Swiss Quality Hotels International.

voyage.name: Grand-Pré Hotel
voyage.content: Four-star hotel, was under Swiss Quality banner but no longer listed there, and may not be open.

voyage.name: Hotel Mon-Repos
voyage.content: Three-star superior hotel situated close to UN and botanic gardens.

voyage.name: Hotel N'vY
voyage.content: Arty, renovated mid-range hotel. Internet is included. Good location close to the lake.

voyage.name: Hotel Ibis Genève Centre Gare
voyage.content: A typical clean chain hotel, with basic room facilities. The hotel is centrally located, yet on a quiet street so it's a great base for weekend sightseeing travellers.

voyage.name: Residence La Reserve
voyage.address: 1 Avenue du Jura, Ferney Voltaire France
voyage.content: Pleasant 4-star hotel with garden, gym and swimming pool. Free wifi internet. Suites & studios with small kitchens. Take bus F to the airport or downtown Geneva.

voyage.name: Les Armures
voyage.content: Lovely 17th-century building in the old town with notable guest list, rooms modern Scandinavian-style.

voyage.name: Beau Rivage
voyage.content: Grand old five-star hotel with beautiful interior, old European style, impeccable service. Outstanding restaurants & choice of vintage wines. In 1898 Empress Elisabeth of Austria stayed here, but she was stabbed by an anarchist on the promenade outside and died.

voyage.name: Four Seasons Hotel Des Bergues
voyage.content: The oldest of Geneva's super-luxury hotels, this palace faces the old town from a superb central right-bank position. A favourite among European royalty.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Kempinski
voyage.content: Very modern and luxurious 5-star hotel, popular with corporate clients. Features a mini-mall, health club and conference rooms.

voyage.name: Hotel President Wilson
voyage.content: Modern five-star hotel, bright decor and many rooms with lake view. Popular with UN staff and Arab families, has one of the best Lebanese restaurants in town.

voyage.name: Hotel Metropole Geneva
voyage.content: Five-star hotel with nice old ambiance, good service. Faces the Jardin Anglais, but for views of the lake or jet d'eau take a room on 3rd floor or higher (one of the suites).

voyage.name: Le Richemond
voyage.content: Five-star hotel in Art Deco style. With restaurant & spa. The Royal Armleder Suite rates as one of the top ten most expensive suites in the world.
